description:
1. Recursively search /working for any entry named "workspace", verify any matches are regular files (not directories or links), and write a single-line indicator containing either "yes" or "no" to "/tmp/workspace_exists" reflecting whether such a regular file was found.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Recursively locate every filesystem entry named "workspace" under /working, determine for each match whether it is a regular file, and save a concise listing of matched paths with their file type to a file named "workspace_matches.txt" in the current directory.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Recursively inspect the /working directory for a regular file named "workspace" and record the result by writing a single line with either "yes" or "no" into the file "/tmp/workspace_presence.flag".

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Recursively search under /working for any regular file named "workspace" and record each found path into a file named "found_workspace_paths.txt" (create that file empty if no matches).

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
